passage: In a dorm room in Warsaw, Emil and Wei opened the order log again. Their delivery service for student errands had been slow all autumn: a parcel here, a shopping run there. But tonight, sorting by date, Wei pointed. "Look at these bunches. December, January, June. Nearly everything is print jobs, and always the week before exams." Emil scrolled. "Lecture notes. People print them and hate queueing." They stopped the errands. For two days they wrote a plan: upload notes, choose a pickup time, collect from a locker outside the library. In the next exam period, orders tripled. Wei laughed at the counter. "We did not lose the idea. We just found the part people wanted."

qa.q: In which months did Wei notice bunches of print jobs?
qa.a: Wei noticed bunches of print jobs in December, January and June.

qa.q: What is Wei feeling when pointing at the bunches in the log?
qa.a: Wei feels a spark of excitement and discovery, pointing quickly as a pattern shows up in the data.

qa.q: What alternative approach could the founders use to check the new focus, and why?
qa.a: They could ask a few students what they would pay for printing and pickup, because the log shows what happened but not what students would keep using.

qa.q: How might a student with exams next week see the new service?
qa.a: A student uploads notes, picks a pickup time and collects them from a locker, so the student avoids the queue during a stressful week.

grounding: Shows adaptive replanning: noticing what customers actually used and narrowing the service to notes and printing, after which orders grew.
